content.value_statement: Large coding changes often fail when scope, design, and acceptance criteria are vague. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through requirements, design, tasks, and staged confirmation.
actual_capabilities: Decides when a full specification workflow is appropriate for medium or large changes.
Creates requirements documents with user stories, scope, non-goals, and EARS acceptance criteria.
Creates design documents covering architecture, module boundaries, data, API, security, and testing notes.
Creates task plans that map implementation work back to requirements.
Requires user confirmation before moving between requirements, design, task planning, and implementation.
limitations: It does not implement code until the user confirms the task plan.
It is not intended for small bug fixes, simple config changes, or one-file documentation edits.
It depends on the agent's project understanding and may require follow-up questions.
It only references sibling design and data-model guidance when those files or URLs are available.

use_cases.title: Define a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn an unclear feature request into user stories, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and review checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Plan a Multi-Module Refactor
use_cases.description: Map architecture decisions, module boundaries, testing needs, and implementation tasks before code changes begin.

use_cases.title: Prepare a UI-Heavy Change
use_cases.description: Clarify user flows, design intent, data needs, and task sequencing for complex interface work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Feature Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spec-workflow to plan a new feature. First ask any missing scope questions, then draft requirements with EARS acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Technical Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the confirmed requirements to create a design document. Include architecture, module boundaries, data flow, security notes, and test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Break Design Into Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the approved design into an implementation plan. Keep each task reviewable and link tasks back to requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide this medium-sized change through requirements, design, task planning, and execution. Stop for confirmation before each phase transition.

output_examples.input: Plan a booking workflow with unclear validation rules.
output: A requirements section with scope, user stories, and EARS acceptance criteria.
A design section covering validation flow, data model impact, and test strategy.
A task checklist tied to the approved requirements.

output_examples.input: Prepare a refactor that touches authentication, billing, and notifications.
output: A design summary with module boundaries and integration risks.
A phased implementation plan with traceability to requirements.
Explicit checkpoints for user review before coding starts.

best_practices: Use the full workflow only for work with meaningful scope, uncertainty, or cross-module impact.
Keep acceptance criteria testable and tied to user-visible behavior.
Confirm each phase before moving from requirements to design, tasks, or implementation.
anti_patterns: Using the workflow for tiny changes where the user already gave exact instructions.
Writing tasks that are not linked to requirements or user-visible outcomes.
Skipping confirmation before implementation when the design or task plan changed.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for medium or large software changes with unclear scope, architecture decisions, or multiple affected modules.

faq.question: Does it write code immediately?
faq.answer: No. It guides requirements, design, and task planning before implementation begins.

faq.question: What are EARS acceptance criteria?
faq.answer: EARS is a structured format for writing clear system behavior and acceptance conditions.

faq.question: Can it help with UI work?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs agents to include user flows, design intent, and related UI guidance when needed.

faq.question: Is it useful for small fixes?
faq.answer: Usually no. The skill says to skip the full workflow for small, precise, low-risk changes.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
